t: Which of the following substance in the fused/liquid state will liberate H₂ at anode on electrolysis?
s:
Electrolysis of molten CaH₂ produces hydrogen gas at anode.
In CaH₂, hydrogen is present in the form of hydride H−.
Oxidation is loss of electrons and we know oxidation occurs at anode and it is also true that in calcium hydride, hydrogen is present as hydride.
So, H− will loss electron and form H₂ gas at the anode.
